quote: Trend Range Rejection (TRR Forever Model) | In overall Direction | With Condition -> CSER | Over extends (High Volume) into 30m/1hr AOI | LTF Shift at AOI | At 15m interval -> 15m, 30m, 45m, 3m variance | Counter Trend [chart]
interpretation: Canonical TRR spec, five conditions: (1) trade in the overall direction; (2) with condition, 'CSER' (not expanded on screen; the handwritten list in VP2-avoiding_overwhelm 00:05:34 writes 'AOI ... (CS -> ER)', so probably condition-specific entry relativity, an inference); (3) price overextends with high volume into a 30m/1h AOI (candle open/close level); (4) LTF shift at the AOI; (5) the shift occurs at a 15m interval of the hour (:15, :30, :45) with a +/-3 minute tolerance. A counter-trend variant is shown as a separate chart. The name on screen is 'Trend Range Rejection', not 'trending range reversal'.

quote: Trend Range Rejection (TRR Forever Model) | Trade in overall trend range direction | Wait for price at Low of Range, fib | Identify 30m, hourly level | Wait for price to overextended, high volume into low of range AOI | LTF shift at 15m 30m into hour
interpretation: Second on-screen TRR checklist (buy side): trending-range direction; price at the low of the range measured with a fib; a 30m/hourly open-close level; high-volume overextension into that low-of-range AOI; LTF shift at :15 or :30 into the hour. Matches the bonus-video slide but lists only :15/:30 (no :45, no 3m variance).

quote: if I just had to use one setup for the rest of my life, I mean, I wasn't able to do any other type of strategy. This would be it. It's called the trend range rejection, the TRR forever model. ... it can be broken down again into three things. What, where, when, direction, area, timing.
interpretation: Author's preferred single setup. Spoken name 'trend range rejection' matches the slide; the transcription_corrections gloss 'TRR = trending range reversal' should be revised to 'Trend Range Rejection'. Structured as what (direction) / where (area) / when (timing).

quote: In this sort of like trending range example, we have the added benefit of two things. So we're stacking the direction of it making high highs and high lows if we're looking for buys. ... We have the added benefit of the overall direction and the range bound condition.
interpretation: TRR direction = trending range: HH/HL for buys (LH/LL for sells) AND corrections deep enough to be range-bound, so the buy is both with-trend and toward the midpoint. This is a trending-range trade, not a trend trade (bears on OQ-21: trend continuation is not the TRR condition).

quote: ideally you're looking for to create 50 of the previous move and you're looking for buyers in the lower half or sales in the upper half ... where are we in relation to the previous range what is a range range is just a low and a high or high and a low
interpretation: TRR 'where' part 1: price must retrace at least 50% of the previous move (buys in the lower half of the last swing low -> swing high). Here 'range' = simply the previous swing leg (low to high), not the multi-hour MTF range box. The swing points themselves are still chosen visually (OQ-01).

quote: for the second thing we'd be looking for at the you know area of interest it would be like a 30 minute or hourly level you know open close of price so we have our direction from condition highs and lows we have uh air of interest through uh the 50 you know fib mark entering the lower half of the previous range push and then we have the 30 minute alley level
interpretation: TRR 'where' part 2: an AOI at a 30m or hourly candle open/close price, coinciding with the >=50% retracement. For TRR (a pro-trend pullback) the AOI is part of the spec, consistent with E1H-012 (pro trending range uses an AOI). The OQ-07 'AOI optional' default applies to the reversal baseline, not to TRR.

quote: if it's high volume ideally i'd love a reversal 15 minutes in or if it's a bit lower volume 30 minutes in what is high versus low volume if the alley candle opens and just immediately dumps into this like the air of interest and then we have you know around 15 minutes and we have that shift it's a bit like slower we're coming in you know uh to that and then we have that shift you know that could be around like 30 minutes in or 45 minutes in
interpretation: TRR timing depends on volume: the hour opens and dumps straight into the AOI (high volume) -> shift ~15 min in; slower approach (lower volume) -> ~30 or 45 min in. Gives an operational high-volume cue: reaching the AOI immediately after the hourly open. The reversal-model lesson puts acceptable reversals at :22-:52 (best :37), so the :15 TRR entry is outside that window.

quote: so for timing when you're looking for a 50 minute interval 15 or 30 minute sometimes 45 minute reversal with a one minute shift or it could even be a tick shift if it's a bit higher volume or like a one minute high low entry
interpretation: '50 minute interval' = 15-minute interval. The TRR trigger is a shift at :15/:30 (sometimes :45): a 1m shift, a tick-chart shift in higher volume, or a 1m HILO entry.

quote: you can take this counter trend if it's more range bound um but yeah what where when each of those kind of three steps have two we're looking for direction condition um entry relativity and 30 minute hourly level and then for timing it's kind of behavior timing 15 minute intervals and a shift so yeah um two four six
interpretation: TRR = six checks in three pairs: WHAT (direction, condition), WHERE (entry relativity, 30m/hourly level), WHEN (candle-behavior timing at 15m intervals, shift). A counter-trend variant is allowed only when the condition is more range-bound.

quote: a really easy way to find direction and condition is just to use the regression trend tool and let's just say what's the high time frame direction and condition if we go to the past day of price action it looks like pretty clear we're moving bullish making higher highs and high lows
interpretation: He uses TradingView's regression trend tool over a window (past day for HTF, a few hours for MTF) as a visual aid for direction/condition. Later (00:11:21) he says not to rely on it for bounces off the channel. A linear-regression slope/channel over the window is an author-endorsed candidate proxy for direction, not a rule.

On the 1m gold chart the MTF window he measures for the TRR example spans 337 bars = 6h37m (range 35.56 points), inside the 5-12h MTF definition, although he calls it 'the past you know a couple hours'. Supports the 5-12h MTF tier for condition over the handwritten 'MTF=5h' (P2G-19).

quote: we've had this you know high volume impulse you know look at these candles very high volume candles and compared to this pullback we can look for a high low entry
interpretation: 'High volume' is judged relative to the pullback: impulse candles much larger than the pullback candles. Supports a relative candle-range proxy (impulse bar range vs preceding pullback bar range) over absolute thresholds. No number given.

quote: You can put a stop loss below the low or a bit of breathing room.
interpretation: TRR stop: beyond the entry-shift swing low (buys), optionally with extra buffer. Buffer size unspecified.

quote: for target where would we want to target for the next hourly kind of level i know we could just target the high of this range as well so high of this range ... it's with the range it's with the trend um you can't tend to hold it longer because you can expect to create a new high ... i'm still working on a way on how i can maximize you know holding these trades
interpretation: TRR target is not 50% of the extension: the next hourly level or the high of the previous range (swing high), and with-trend trades can be held for a new high. He says the exit method is still unresolved. Consistent with the adaptive rule (E1H-038) and contrasts with the 50% default (E1H-037).

quote: a bit of a you know tick shift high volume shift because it's you know you had a really big impulse into this area of interest you can take a lower time frame entry a one minute at high low that's when you'd be looking for this setup because it's high volume and you'll be entering at the breakout because again it's high volume less likely for it to pull back and it's at a good time around 30 minutes into the hour
interpretation: High volume into the AOI -> lower-timeframe trigger (tick shift / 1m HILO) entered on the breakout, no pullback wait. Example entry ~30 min into the hour.

quote: you have the 50% you know fib point um you can even like yeah from the swing high to swing low this can be a bit you know intuitive ... I mainly use middle time frame. It depends on the type of range, but you know, swing high, swing low, 50% point of that.
interpretation: Choosing the swing high/low for the 50% fib is explicitly 'intuitive' and depends on the range type, mainly MTF swings. Confirms there is no stated pivot rule (OQ-01 stays a research parameter).

quote: for the entry that that shift it could be um you know a one minute like high low entry where you have it you know one a candle um like clearly like break the previous low um and then you know break the next high so one minute uh high low entry that would look like a from breaking low to breaking high
interpretation: 1m HILO entry (buy): price clearly breaks the previous 1m low, then breaks the next high; entry on the high break. Supports the OQ-09 default (a low taken then a high, at 1m-candle scale). Whether the 'high' is the same candle's or the next swing's is not exact.

quote: If it's high volume, the higher the volume it is, the lower time frame you're looking at. The lower the volume, the more likely you'd be wanting to just wait for a one-minute structure shift.
interpretation: Entry-chart choice scales with volume: higher volume -> lower timeframe (tick/seconds/1m HILO); lower volume -> 1m structure shift.

interpretation: In a range the tradable 'direction' is toward the range midpoint; in a trending range either side toward the midpoint, holding longer with the overall direction. Consistent with E15-011/E15-012.

interpretation: Condition = size of pull relative to push. Equal push and pull (~100% correction) = range-bound. Consistent with the >=75-100% range threshold; no numbers given here.

quote: there's four main way like types of conditions we have trending which is more directional um like volatility is more of a range you can range from um you know high volume um down to low volume ... so these are all kind of sliders it's not you know black or white it's it's shades of gray ... this would be like a high volume range where these can be pretty nice to trade but then you can also have like a low volume range which is really nasty
interpretation: Condition is two continuous axes: trend<->range and low<->high volume. High-volume ranges are good; low-volume ranges are 'really nasty'. interpretation: Bad condition = no trade; good condition = more size/trades. In extreme high-volume bullish gold at all-time highs he limits and trades conservatively rather than a strict ban. Evidence for both a gate (bad) and a downgrade (difficult), OQ-21.

Condition -> setup map: directional + high volume -> 0-15 min continuation; range + lower volume -> 30 min reversal; range + high volume -> 15 min reversal. quote: if you're labeling that after um the trade has happened and you know if it's a win or a loss it's meaningless because that there's so much confirmation bias that it doesn't matter if you label the tier of the trade if you label it an a plus trade and you consistently do this before as you enter that trade and then that's actually you know that's not biased data ... this is why ideally you want to enter a trade and then immediately journal that trade
interpretation: Author warns that quality/confluence labels added after the outcome are hindsight-biased. For this project: Level-2 journal tags may be post-hoc, so the win rates they support are claims, and backtest labels must be computed at entry time only.

quote: focus on what's you know the least amount of confluences that give you the most benefit so my like my most effective confluences um is dxy alignment market structure shifts like type three market structure shifts and like some correlation like uh and maybe yeah market alignment ... you don't want to have too many rules too many any confluences otherwise you just you know um you're going to curve fit yourself
interpretation: Most effective confluences per author: DXY alignment, type-3 market-structure shifts, correlation, market(-structure) alignment. Warns against too many rules (curve fitting). Supports a small baseline feature set and ablation-style testing.

You know, we can also add in like DXY correlation or silver correlation, and we can get insane results. This is how I have a 90% win rate on certain setups, ... I'm going to trade gold. It might not be there, but in around that 15 minute, 30 minute candle, I'm going to be looking for reversals.
interpretation: AUTHOR CLAIM: reversals win more in lower-volume range-bound conditions, continuations in directional ones; '90% on certain setups' with correlation added. Daily routine: gold, Asia hour 2, continuation in the first 10 min, reversals around the 15m/30m candles. Silver correlation is out of scope.

That last claim conflicts with his spoken 30m reversals 75-90% vs continuations 46-66%, and the DXY figures conflict with the spoken 61% -> 80%. Treat the slide numbers as illustrative.

quote: So the more data points you have, there's going to be less noise or noise is going to affect your results or your analysis a lot less if you have 300 trades journaled versus only 50 trades journaled. The more data you get, the less noise will matter.
interpretation: Author's own sample-size stance: 300 trades far better than 50 (slides say 100-200 minimum, 50-100 per hypothesis). Useful as a stated minimum for evaluating claimed statistics.

quote: you don't want to refine from trade to trade. You don't even want to refine from week to week. you mainly i think i mainly kind of refine from month to month um you don't want to have too many rules you don't want to curve fit
interpretation: Refinement cadence: monthly, not per trade/week; avoid too many rules (curve fitting). Relevant to walk-forward design (parameter changes at most monthly).

quote: You now know that if I take a trade in the first 10 minutes, it should be a continuation as it increases my win rate by 20%.
interpretation: AUTHOR CLAIM: in the first 10 minutes of the hour, continuations win ~20 percentage points more (than reversals, implied). Consistent with P2G-46 (66% vs 51%).

quote: This is even the same for the first half Asia, like these are 33% win rates. I'm getting fucked in the first half Asia.
interpretation: AUTHOR CLAIM: 33% win rate in the first half of Asia (slide: 'first hour of the Asia session leads to a 33% win rate but improves significantly in the second hour'). Conflicts with E1H-042 listing Asia hour 1 as traded; supports Asia hour 2 as his window (OQ-16).

quote: you want to weight each confluence by each condition so maybe continuations only work like work really well when it's more directional or trending because obviously you're moving further one direction but if it's more range bound and you're trying to take a break and retest it's unlikely to play out because it's going to range
interpretation: Confluences should be weighted per condition (interaction effects). Supports condition-segmented evaluation (condition x setup) rather than one global filter (OQ-21 B).

quote: Example: A trader reviewing data might find that trading during the first hour of the Asia session leads to a 33% win rate but improves significantly in the second hour. ... Example: A trader realized that taking trades on candles without wicks had only a 35% win rate, while trades with wick rejection increased to 73%. This led to an adjustment to avoid setups without clear wick formations.
interpretation: Slide claims (template-like 'a trader'): Asia hour 1 33% vs better hour 2; no-wick candles 35% vs wick rejection 73%. Spoken version says the inverse no-wick setup 'hadn't lost' (00:10:32). Numbers differ slightly from speech (38%).

quote: no mechanical system works for manual traders um it's insanely difficult um so uh if you're looking for a purely mechanical system where you don't have to think or use your discretion unfortunately you probably just shouldn't be trading because that is how we actually get that edge um you need that discretion that intuition that gut feeling
interpretation: Author holds that his edge is discretionary application to condition, not the mechanical rules. For this project: a mechanical CBR/TRR baseline is a formalization the author would not endorse as equivalent; failure of the baseline does not refute his claims, and success is not his method verbatim.

quote: I have a systematic discretionary approach. my intuition in a kind of mechanical way. So I'm still using discretion, intuition to apply it to the right conditions, but I'm more mechanical in how I do it. I'm more systematic. I look to validate parts of my intuition by using lots of data or collecting lots of data and set rules and limitations around that
interpretation: Systematic-discretionary: condition selection is intuitive; execution rules and limits are systematic and data-validated.

quote: if i'm taking like a type 3 shift here like a market structure shift where we go from breaking highs to breaking lows here looking to take a sell stop above previous high targeting previous low
interpretation: Generic type-3 sell: structure goes from breaking highs to breaking lows; stop above the previous high; target the previous low. A structural target (previous swing), not 50% of extension.

quote: the best continuations tend to be in the first 10 minutes of the hour
interpretation: Continuations: best in the first 10 minutes of the hour (later: 'first two to ten minutes but it depends on type of condition', 00:05:41). Narrows the 0-15 min window of E1H-026.

quote: looking at how you're moving prior to the open of the hour, we overall are extremely bullish here. So trending range type of thing, but we have a big pullback prior to the open, that means it's more likely to open and immediately push in that direction. ... you need to be mindful of how you you know move at the last 10 minutes of the prior alley candle
interpretation: A pullback during the last ~10 minutes of the previous hour makes the new hour more likely to open and push immediately with the trend (no opposite wick). A candidate timing feature: prior-hour last-10-min direction vs trend.

quote: if you push too much like if you push way too much without you know much of a pullback at all that can actually signal that it's more likely to reverse like price has overextended you're more likely to have a reversal to then correct and fill in that move so in this example here we have it open a big push downwards downwards and then press like to correct fill in that move.
interpretation: Even inside a high-volume trend, a push with almost no pullback signals overextension and a likely corrective reversal. This is the same logic as CBR, applied inside a trend.

quote: you're not going to get any you know 15 30 minute reversals it's really tricky because it's so much volume you're just continuing to push in one direction there's so much volume um you wouldn't want to blindly take sales you'd have you want to wait for a clear shift in market structure to then take a sell so respecting lows respecting lows expecting lows you can still take reversals but um you have to wait for a clear shift in market structure and even still uh you're gonna have to be you know pretty conservative with the take profit
interpretation: In very high-volume trends 15/30-minute reversals are unreliable; a reversal needs a clear market-structure shift and a conservative target. This is a downgrade (stricter trigger, smaller target), not an absolute ban (OQ-21 B), while E1H-046 says ideally don't trade.

quote: i think it's just easier if you just always look for um like buying in the lower half selling the other half of the previous move so i'm not looking to buy until we pull back into the lower half regardless of the condition so that just means if it's a high volume um like condition here um like i'm waiting for it to pull back when it doesn't pull back i just don't take a trade ... i don't trade really high volume because i wait for pullback and then that pullback never comes
interpretation: His practical filter: buy only after price reaches the lower half of the previous move (sell upper half) regardless of condition; high-volume trends are skipped automatically because the pullback never comes. Operationalizes OQ-21 through an entry-relativity >=50% requirement instead of a separate trend gate.

quote: condition specific trading is more intuitive it's more subjective because it's just there's an infinite amount of detail and little things that you need to train your your mind to see so i can't give you you know purely mechanical rules based things
interpretation: Author explicitly declines to give mechanical condition rules. Any numeric condition classifier (OQ-02) is a research interpretation; confidence in condition labels must stay lowered.

quote: for me i trade mainly pullbacks um so i like ranges i like trending ranges i have a higher win rate off reversals which you know um most people you know think you should just be taking continuations but you should only be taking continuations when the condition allows that
interpretation: AUTHOR CLAIM: higher win rate on reversals; he mainly trades pullbacks in ranges and trending ranges. Supports focusing the baseline on range/trending-range conditions.

quote: with continuations when it's more directional more trending you can just look for breaks and retests you know where are you looking for a break and retest is that the previous low ... you're just looking for a continuation around that midpoint so around you know correction half of that previous move That is where the best sort of continuations tap into.
interpretation: Continuation entry in directional conditions: break-and-retest of the previous swing, ideally at ~50% correction of the previous move. Out of the reversal baseline; relevant to a continuation model.

quote: we just zoom out quite a lot and you only really need one time frame. using the one minute as they all show the same thing
interpretation: All duration tiers (LTF/MTF/HTF) are read from the 1m chart by zooming. Supports deriving swings for all tiers from 1m data (OQ-01 option C).

quote: We've got like a one minute type two shift bullish, we broke a low, broke a high.
interpretation: A 1m 'type two' shift is described as 'broke a low, broke a high', the same verbal pattern used elsewhere for a type-3 shift (E1H-030) and for HILO (P2G-17). Types 1/2/3 therefore cannot be distinguished from speech. OQ-09 stays unresolved; the difference is probably drawn on screen or defined in the other analyst's shift videos.

quote: we can look for a pullback um and kind of how we were talking about on the previous example uh we can look for the midpoint of this previous move um for a reaction in that hopefully it pulls back into that midpoint so we have that midpoint reaction and look for an entry, stop below the previous low, and we can target maybe some of these previous highs
interpretation: Aligned-structure pullback trade: wait for a reaction at the midpoint (50%) of the previous move, enter, stop below the previous low, target previous highs.

quote: remember you can just take a trade with two time frames aligning If it's high time from counter trend though You are you only want to be doing this counter trend selling a near highs has to be selling their highs ... that's what i'm you know mainly focused at the moment is making sure I align low time frame with middle time frame sometimes high time frame as well uh you just want two two or three um three is better
interpretation: Minimum alignment = 2 tiers (LTF with MTF); 3 is better. If the trade is counter to HTF, it must be near highs for sells (lows for buys), i.e. external/extreme location. Consistent with E15-011.

quote: it's not like fixed it's not like is this middle time frame yes or no it's like how much of a middle time frame is this
interpretation: Duration tiers are fuzzy, not fixed windows. Supports testing tier windows as parameters (OQ-03).

quote: i'm looking at low time frame middle time from high time frame market structure alignment has to be you know relative to the condition for areas of interest there's 30 minute hourly levels and the entry has to be relative to the previous move it has to be relative to the condition so if it's ranging need to be you know buying the lows selling the highs if it's high volume buying their highs selling their lows ... if it's trending zero to 50 minute continuations if it's ranging 15 30 minute reversals market structure type three shifts and one minute high lows
interpretation: Most detailed level of his 3-step what/where/when method: LTF/MTF/HTF alignment relative to condition; 30m/hourly AOI; entry relative to previous move and condition (ranging: buy lows / sell highs; high volume: buy highs / sell lows, i.e. breakouts); timing: trending -> 0-15 min continuations, ranging -> 15-30 min reversals; triggers: type-3 shifts and 1m HILOs. 'High volume buying highs' conflicts with his own 'always wait for the lower half' (P2G-65).

interpretation: Slide summary: MS alignment over LTF/MTF/HTF and 2-3 conditions; 30m/hourly levels with condition-relative entry; CB hour timing by condition with shift/HILO at 15m intervals; 'Correlation just for entry confirmation'. Supports DXY as a confirmation/timing input rather than a condition veto (OQ-13).
